# Implementation Plan: MVP - Add and Manage Feed Subscriptions

**Branch**: `001-add-subscriptions` | **Date**: 2026-04-08 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/001-add-subscriptions/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command. Phase 0 (research) and Phase 1 (design) execute during plan generation.

## Summary

MVP subscription management system: Users can add RSS/Atom feed URLs and view a list of subscriptions in a web application. Backend stores subscriptions in memory; frontend displays them in a simple UI. Technical approach: ASP.NET Core Web API backend with Blazor WebAssembly frontend, in-memory storage, no feed fetching or persistence for MVP phase. Architecture supports incremental addition of feed parsing and persistence in Extended-MVP without requiring redesign.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: C# / .NET 7 or 8 (latest LTS)  
**Primary Dependencies**: 
- Backend: ASP.NET Core Web API, minimal dependencies for MVP
- Frontend: Blazor WebAssembly, no external UI frameworks (use HTML/CSS)
**Storage**: In-memory List<Subscription> for MVP (no database)  
**Testing**: xUnit for unit tests; manual integration testing during development  
**Target Platform**: Windows, macOS, Linux (cross-platform .NET Core runtime)
**Project Type**: Web application (frontend + backend separation)  
**Performance Goals**: Add subscription and display list within 1 second; UI responsive with 50+ subscriptions; sub-100ms API response times  
**Constraints**: Single-user, local-only, no production security requirements for MVP; in-memory data lost on restart  
**Scale/Scope**: MVP demonstrates only subscription management (2 user stories); supports < 100 subscriptions during development

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Principle I - Security & Input Safety
**Status**: ✅ PASS  
**Verification**: 
- Feed URLs will be basic strings (no parsing required for MVP)
- CORS will be explicitly configured in backend Program.cs
- No credentials or secrets in code
- Input safety deferred to Extended-MVP when feed fetching begins

### Principle II - Clean Separation of Concerns
**Status**: ✅ PASS  
**Verification**:
- Frontend (Blazor) responsible for UI only
- Backend (ASP.NET Core) handles subscription storage and API
- Communication via documented HTTP API contract (POST for add, GET for list)
- No business logic duplication

### Principle III - Code Quality & Maintainability
**Status**: ✅ PASS  
**Verification**:
- Meaningful method and class names (SubscriptionService, AddSubscription, etc.)
- YAGNI enforced: only in-memory storage for MVP, no unnecessary persistence layer
- Tech stack choices documented in TechStack.md
- Deferred features (feed fetching, persistence) clearly tracked

### Principle IV - Testing & Quality Gates
**Status**: ⚠️ PASS WITH GUIDANCE  
**Verification**:
- Unit tests for SubscriptionService (add, retrieve)
- Integration tests for API endpoints (POST add, GET list)
- Manual testing of full workflow before completion
- Test gaps for feed parsing deferred to Extended-MVP

### Principle V - MVP-First Incremental Development
**Status**: ✅ PASS  
**Verification**:
- Scope strictly limited to subscription management
- Architecture designed for additive extension (feed fetching is separate)
- No future-proofing complexity
- Extended-MVP adds only feed service and item display

**Overall**: ✅ ALL GATES PASS - Proceed to Phase 0 research

### Source Code (repository root)

**Architecture**: Web application (ASP.NET Core + Blazor WebAssembly)

```text
backend/
├── RSSFeedReader.Api/
│   ├── Controllers/
│   │   └── SubscriptionsController.cs    # API endpoints for subscriptions
│   ├── Models/
│   │   └── Subscription.cs               # Subscription entity (id, url, dateAdded)
│   ├── Services/
│   │   └── SubscriptionService.cs        # Business logic: add, retrieve subscriptions
│   ├── Program.cs                        # Dependency injection, CORS config
│   └── Properties/
│       └── launchSettings.json           # Port 5151 (HTTP), 7151 (HTTPS)
└── RSSFeedReader.Api.Tests/
    ├── Unit/
    │   └── SubscriptionServiceTests.cs   # Test add/retrieve logic
    └── Integration/
        └── SubscriptionsControllerTests.cs # Test API endpoints

frontend/
├── RSSFeedReader.UI/
│   ├── Pages/
│   │   └── Subscriptions.razor           # Main MVP page: input + list
│   ├── Services/
│   │   └── SubscriptionApiService.cs     # HTTP client for backend API
│   ├── Layout/
│   │   ├── MainLayout.razor              # App shell
│   │   └── NavMenu.razor                 # Navigation (updated for MVP)
│   ├── wwwroot/
│   │   ├── appsettings.json              # API base URL: http://localhost:5151/api/
│   │   └── css/app.css                   # Basic styling
│   ├── Program.cs                        # BlazorWebAssembly bootstrap
│   └── Properties/
│       └── launchSettings.json           # Port 5213 (HTTP), 7213 (HTTPS)
└── RSSFeedReader.UI.Tests/
    └── Integration/
        └── SubscriptionWorkflowTests.cs  # Test add subscription → display list
```

**Structure Decision**: Web application pattern selected (backend API + Blazor frontend) based on technology stack mandate in TechStack.md. Separation of concerns enables independent testing and scaling. Port configuration: Backend 5151, Frontend 5213, coordinated via appsettings.json and CORS policy.
